posts.title: Standard Equation: $y^2 = 4ax$
posts.body: A parabola is the locus of a point whose distance from the focus $(a, 0)$ equals its perpendicular distance from the directrix $x = -a$. Here eccentricity $e = 1$.
posts.analogy: Like a satellite dish focusing every parallel incoming signal ray onto a single detector point.

posts.title: Latus Rectum Length: $4a$
posts.body: The chord passing through focus $(a,0)$ and perpendicular to the axis of symmetry has endpoints $(a, 2a)$ and $(a, -2a)$. Total length is $|4a|$.
posts.analogy: The focal aperture width determining how wide or narrow the bowl opens.

posts.title: Board MCQ: Focus Coordinates
posts.body: Given the parabola $y^2 = -16x$, find the coordinates of its focus.

quiz.question: What is the focus of the parabola $y^2 = -16x$?
quiz.explanation: Comparing with $y^2 = -4ax$, we get $4a = 16 \implies a = 4$. Since the parabola opens leftwards, focus is $(-a, 0) = (-4, 0)$.

posts.title: Suspension Bridges & Headlight Reflectors
posts.body: Cables of suspension bridges like the Bandra-Worli Sea Link hang in parabolic curves under uniform floor loading. Parabolic reflectors bounce bulb rays into a parallel beam.
posts.analogy: Real-world Mumbai civil engineering shaped by quadratic geometry.

posts.title: Board Trap: Upward vs Downward Parabola
posts.body: For $x^2 = 4ay$, the axis is the y-axis, not x-axis! Directrix is $y = -a$. Never confuse horizontal $y^2=4ax$ with vertical $x^2=4ay$.

posts.title: Board MCQ: Tangent in Slope Form
posts.body: What is the condition for line $y = mx + c$ to be tangent to parabola $y^2 = 4ax$?

quiz.question: Which relation gives the condition of tangency for $y = mx + c$ and $y^2 = 4ax$?
quiz.explanation: Substituting $y = mx + c$ and setting the quadratic discriminant $\Delta = 0$ gives $c = \frac{a}{m}$.
